advice: Experiment: make the existing A transpose cache-blocked for all n. Keep its ZA loads and transpose stores, but process a small block of adjacent output-row tiles across a bounded range of k tiles before moving on. Choose the block dimensions from the current SME vector length and keep every address predicate-bounded. Preserve the existing transposed layout at[k*n+i] and the consumption kernel unchanged. Hypothesis: reuse row-major A cache lines across nearby transpose work and reduce transpose-side cache misses, while retaining the full transpose that lets the GEMM reuse A across column tiles. Compare complete gemm time, including allocation, transpose, and consumption, against the incumbent for supported sizes; do not infer a benefit from the transpose phase alone.
risks: This may add loop and predicate overhead, increase the transpose working set, or disrupt ZA scheduling. Cache-blocking may help some sizes and hurt others; a single block size may not suit all n. Keep the ABI, FP32 arithmetic, reduction order, thread count, tolerance, benchmark, and selector use unchanged. No gain is established by the supplied noisy trials, and the earlier fused-transpose proposal's severe regression argues against repeating that same change.
